hook: From *tomorrow*: builders get sewage-treated water, borewells need MRO nod
hook_b: Digging a borewell near a public tap? You now need *MRO permission*
tldr: From Nov 1, HMWSSB's green tankers supply treated wastewater, and borewells near drinking sources need MRO permission.

beats.what: HMWSSB starts green water tankers on Nov 1. Borewells near public drinking water sources need prior MRO permission.
beats.why: Hyderabad's reservoirs are low, so drinking water is being saved for homes.
beats.care: Building or digging a borewell? Get MRO clearance first. Sites must switch to treated-water tankers.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Green water tankers start Sunday, Nov 1. They carry treated water from sewage treatment plants for industry, construction and gardening. Civic bodies, government agencies and public spaces get it first. Registrations and filling points are still being set up. Separately, a borewell near a public drinking water source now needs prior permission from the Mandal Revenue Officer (MRO). Officials will inspect sites to enforce distance norms. The exact distance and fees were not in the report.

cards.title: 🧠 Why now
cards.body: Most of the city already gets tap water once every 3 days under emergency rules. The green tankers are meant to keep drinking water for homes by giving builders, industry and gardens treated water instead.
